features.title: Clause roles and finite predicates
features.scope_note: Identify complete clauses, finite predicate, expressed/understood subject and governed complements by morphology, agreement and frame; order is corroboration, not the sole criterion.

features.title: Main-clause fronting
features.scope_note: Subject-initial and fronted main clauses; second constituent is not second written word. Finite-second is an evidenced tendency, with actual exceptions; no automatic transformation.

features.title: Pronoun position and limits
features.scope_note: A subject pronoun may precede the finite verb after a fronted adverbial: exact Æfter ðon hē underðēodde. Neither pronouns nor fronting impose an exceptionless placement rule.

features.title: Sustained reference and ambiguity
features.scope_note: Recover antecedents through agreement, syntax, discourse and meaning. Masculine sang can be referred to by hē/hine; identical masculine candidates can remain ambiguous. Do not choose nearest noun mechanically.

features.title: Coordination and predicate recovery
features.scope_note: Recover a shared subject or repeated lexical predicate only where the clauses support it. Restore finite agreement with the second expressed subject: singular wæs becomes plural wǣron. Cook134.1–2 independently has singular cymð and omitted plural coming.

features.title: Person in reported and quoted speech
features.scope_note: Within direct quotation, first and second person refer to current speaker and addressees. In indirect report, contextual third-person reference can be explicit or ambiguous; mood does not identify the antecedent.

features.title: Long-sentence analysis
features.scope_note: Find boundaries and finite predicates before resolving reference; keep embedded clauses and coordinated material separate; return to apposition and source notes where necessary.

features.title: Long fronting in the source
features.scope_note: Recognition only with explicit help: Cook152.8–9 Ðā stefne and ðone sang are accusatives governed by embedded gehīerde, as note8 says. Do not teach them as ordinary objects of cwæð or license free long extraction.

features.title: Dependent clause order
features.scope_note: Dependent finite predicates often occur late/end, but need not be last. Cook25.7 expressly asks verb last for that item; this is a target constraint, not a general validity test.

features.title: Correlative and homographic clause markers
features.scope_note: Reuse taught temporal/causal relatives and correlatives. Distinguish temporal conjunction ðā, main adverb ðā, and demonstrative/article ðā by construction, agreement and context; paired when/then can clarify. No universal inversion diagnostic.

features.title: Negation and questions in clause analysis
features.scope_note: Reuse ne plus finite, negative concord, interrogative-word and finite-initial yes/no questions; existing forms/moods only. This reinforces earlier systems and does not silently add contracted negative copulas.

rules.statement: Selected long-form weak II: -ie, -ast, -að, -iað; preterite -ode, -odest, -ode, -odon. Infinitive -ian, inflected -ianne, present participle -iende, past -od. Alternative -ige/-ade formations remain outside this selected system.
Weak I has selected present stems and dental preterite; syncope and consonant outcomes are stated per lexical row. Full singular/plural indicative endings follow §117.

The selected āstręccean system has geminate/ungeminated present alternation and unmutated preterite āstreahte. Past is not mechanically generated from the mutated infinitive. Source154 verifies āstreahte; §114 supports the lexical class.

Strong III four stems govern present, past1/3 singular, past2 singular/plural, and past participle. Selected mutations eor→ier before 2/3 singular endings follow Cook; forceorfan ier is declared Cook-style normalization of BT cirf/cyrf variants. n+st simplifies to -nst, nn+ð to -nð.
Strong VII lexical pasts hēold and ondrēd are learned with their stems. Dental-ending simplifications in present follow Wright§476; imperative singular drops doubled/final consonant as appropriate.
Strong II bēod/bēad/bud/bod; present2/3 singular bīetst/bīett follows checked Cook§103. Only attested bebēodan prefix identity is licensed.
Lexically attested fordōn and ingān take the checked dōn/gān finite morphology with their prefixes. ingangan/ingangende is a separately supplied lexical variant, not a regular ingān participle.
Selected plain infinitive plus -ne after its final n gives the inflected infinitive -anne/-enne (including -ianne). Promote a prior citation form only through the explicit pair.
